text:
maya: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-picker tweak I’m seeing a ~12% drop in prefix hit-rate for a specific customer workload. Not a bulk regen, looks like client-side opt-in headers are being ignored in some retry+stream flows.

glen: Oof. Do you have an example request/headers?

maya: Here’s a minimal repro curl we used from the SDK tests:

```\ncurl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"X-Redwood-Cache-Opt: true\" \\n  -H \"X-Redwood-Prefix-Key: sess-1234::user_prompt_v2\" \\n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate\n```

maya: Server logs show the request landed on a runtime instance with new kernel selection logic and then a retry from the client within ~80ms (stream started then reconnect). The runtime metric `prefix_cache.hit` is 0 for the first attempt and 1 for the retry. But overall hit-rate drops because warmups happen on the instance that never actually returns the primary stream.

priya: Can you paste the log snippet where headers are parsed? I want to see canonicalization codepath.

maya: Sure — redacted logs:

```\n[2026-03-18T15:02:10.123Z] req=abcd1234 headers={authorization:****, x-redwood-prefix-key: sess-1234::user_prompt_v2, x-redwood-cache-opt: true}\n[2026-03-18T15:02:10.204Z] kernel-select: selected kernel=batchA seq=512\n[2026-03-18T15:02:10.207Z] attempt=1 stream=started instance=i-rt-07 parsing-headers -> cache-opt header not found\n[2026-03-18T15:02:10.289Z] client-retry idempotency=none attempt=2 -> cache lookup hit=true\n```

maya: See "cache-opt header not found" even though request shows x-redwood-cache-opt in the raw headers. It seems parsing code checks for `X-Redwood-Cache-Opt` with exact-case somewhere after kernel-select path. New kernel codepath uses a lower-level http parser that returns header names lowercased, but downstream check is case-sensitive.

samir: That would explain why the warmup happened on the retried connection only. Also if streaming starts and partial KV segments are written by the first attempt, the retry ends up hitting a partially populated prefix in a different instance -> miss storms.

glen: Two problems then: header canonicalization mismatch and streaming+retry write race for KV warmups. Both could reduce global hit-rate and increase tail latency.

priya: Quick mitigation: 1) normalize header names to lowercase at the front of the runtime HTTP handler (cheap). 2) hold off writing prefix warmups until stream finalization or require idempotency token to mark warmup writes.

maya: Agreed. I ran a quick patch locally to lowercase incoming header keys before any decision logic — local synthetic workload recovered hit-rate to baseline. Patch diff:

```\n- if (req.headers[\"X-Redwood-Cache-Opt\"] === \"true\") {\n+ const hdr = lowercasedHeaders(req.headers);\n+ if (hdr[\"x-redwood-cache-opt\"] === \"true\") {\n    enablePrefixWarmup();\n}\n```

maya: Also added a small gated flag `warmup_on_stream_commit` that defaults to false; toggling it prevented partial-write races in the test harness.

samir: Nice. How does this interplay with kernel selection? Any perf cost to normalizing earlier in the pipeline?

glen: Normalizing is a trivial string op — negligible. But kernel selection currently probes sequence-length/dispatch metrics early; we must ensure we don't delay that by moving heavy blocking ops earlier. The lowercase op is constant-time and fine.

maya: I ran a 10k request A/B: baseline vs header-normalize-only vs header-normalize+defer-warmup. Results: hit-rate: baseline 78.3% -> normalize 86.7% -> normalize+defer 91.2%. Tail latency p95 improved ~40ms in final config. Pushing the CL now.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: PR #4128 -> staging -> smoke tests -> canary 10%.

priya: After canary I'll follow with a small metric to detect 'partial warmup writes' — count of warmup-writes where stream was not completed within 500ms. If >0.5% of writes we rollback.

maya: Filed follow-up: create SDK test that sends header variants (Cache-Opt: true, cache-opt: true, X-Redwood-Cache-Opt: true) to ensure our SDK canonicalization matches server. Also added a note to the API docs for the canonical header names and recommended SDK helper.

glen: Excellent. Nice detective work. :tada:

maya: TL;DR: kernel-picker change exposed a header-canonicalization bug + streaming retry race. Fix: lowercase headers in runtime and gate warmup writes until commit (or require idempotency token). Canary in progress.
